copy.reflect_ref_apologized_agreed: Saying sorry and agreeing when you don't mean it makes the discomfort stop for now. The need doesn't go away. It goes quiet.
copy.reflect_ref_apologized_quiet: Saying sorry and then going quiet can be something people learn when asking felt risky. Your voice is still there.
copy.reflect_ref_crying_cried: Tears in a hard talk usually mean it matters to you. The skill is keeping going through them, or saying 'I need a minute' without dropping what you need.
copy.reflect_ref_crying_froze: Tears and freezing can come when there's too much to hold at once. Next time you can give yourself permission to pause.
copy.reflect_ref_default: Whatever happened in that moment, you did the best you could with what you had. Let's find something you can reach for next time.
copy.reflect_ref_defensive_froze: When someone gets defensive, freezing is common. The skill isn't never freezing. It's having a plan for when you do.
copy.reflect_ref_defensive_loud: When they got defensive, you matched their intensity. That happens to most people. The aim is to notice the surge a moment before it takes over.
copy.reflect_ref_defensive_quiet: Going quiet when someone gets defensive can be a way to protect yourself. The question is whether the quiet helped you, or only kept the peace.
copy.reflect_ref_escalated_left: Leaving when things escalate can be a skill. One sentence can turn it into a break: 'I need to pause. I want to come back to this.'
copy.reflect_ref_escalated_loud: When it escalated and you got louder, you were trying to be heard. Volume usually makes it harder for the other person to hear you.
copy.reflect_ref_gavein_agreed: Giving in to keep the peace makes sense when conflict feels risky. Peace paid for with your needs costs a lot. A plan for next time can help you hold on a little longer, when it's safe to.
copy.reflect_ref_gavein_left: Leaving can be a wise move, especially before saying something you'd regret. If you want to come back to it, a plan for that can help.
copy.reflect_ref_nowords_changed: Changing the subject when the words wouldn't come was a way out of the moment. One rehearsed sentence can be there for you next time.
copy.reflect_ref_nowords_froze: When feelings flood in, words are hard to reach. It's not that you had nothing to say. A few lines ready ahead of time can help.
copy.reflect_ref_okay_stayed: You stayed on course, so something worked. Was it something you said, something you didn't say, or something you did with your body?
copy.rehearse_ca_apology_check: When you feel the urge to say sorry, pause and ask: 'Did I do something wrong, or am I uncomfortable?' If it's discomfort, try 'I know this is hard' instead of 'I'm sorry'. Practise the swap now. Or come back to it later.
copy.rehearse_ca_body_anchor: When you notice the signal: feet on the floor, hands on your thighs, one slow breath. It buys you a couple of seconds to think. Try it now: feet, hands, breath. Or come back to it later.
copy.rehearse_ca_broken_record: Pick your one key sentence, the thing you need to say. When the talk starts spinning, come back to it. Same words, calm voice: 'What I need is…' Say it three times now, a little softer each time. Or come back to it later.
copy.rehearse_ca_name_the_dynamic: When things heat up, name the pattern instead of the content: 'I notice we're both getting louder. I don't want that. Can we slow down?' Say it out loud now. Or come back to it later.
copy.rehearse_ca_pause_phrase: Choose one sentence for when you feel the moment coming, like 'I want to keep talking about this. I need a second.' Say it out loud three times now. Notice how it feels to say. Or come back to it later.
copy.rehearse_ca_planned_exit: Choose your exit line now: 'I care about this too much to keep going while we're both this upset. Can we come back to it at [a time]?' Naming a time makes it a pause, not an escape. Say it out loud. Or come back to it later.
copy.rehearse_ca_success_anchor: You stayed on course. Before it fades, describe what you did with your body, your voice, and where you put your attention. Write it down. That's your playbook for next time. Or come back to it later.
copy.rehearse_ca_tears_plan: Give yourself permission ahead of time: 'If I cry, that's okay. I'll keep talking.' You could tell them: 'I might get emotional. It doesn't mean I want to stop.' Say that now and notice what comes up. Or come back to it later.
copy.rehearse_ca_time_limit: Before you start, say: 'I'd like to talk about this for 15 minutes, then check how we're both doing.' A time limit makes a hard talk feel more doable, and gives you a natural place to stop. Or come back to it later.
copy.rehearse_ca_validate_first: Before you say what you need, name what they might be feeling: 'I can see this is hard for you too.' One line like that can lower their guard. Say it now. Or come back to it later.
copy.rehearse_ca_write_it_down: Write down the two or three things you want to say. It's not a script. It's something to glance at if the words go. Do it now, on your phone or on paper. Or come back to it later.

copy.accept_line: Most of this is facts or other people's choices. That's painful, and it isn't a failure. Here the skill is to carry it, not solve it.
copy.ack_anger: Your anger says something that mattered got crossed. Let's work out what to do about it.
copy.ack_disgust: Something is crossing a line for you. Let's see what you can do about it.
copy.ack_envy: Envy points at something you want. That's useful to know, and you can use it.
copy.ack_fear: Your fear is pointing at something that matters to you. Let's see what you can do about it.
copy.ack_guilt: Something you did doesn't sit right with your values. The move now is repair, not punishing yourself.
copy.ack_jealousy: Something in this relationship feels under threat. Let's look at what you can do, starting from what you need.
copy.ack_love: The love is real, and something is in the way. Let's look at what's in the way.
copy.ack_routed: Something is asking a lot of you right now. Let's see what you can do about it.
copy.ack_sadness: You've lost something, or something didn't go the way you needed. Let's see which parts you can do something about.
copy.ambiv_title: What does staying the same protect you from?
copy.barrier_hint: There's no wrong answer. It helps find the next step.
copy.barrier_title: What's in the way of doing something about it?
copy.co_high: So the how is there. Let's name the step.
copy.co_low: That's honest. Someone else could help with this, and a smaller piece might be in reach.
copy.co_medium: Small is real. Let's find the smallest version that still counts.
copy.co_none: Then the step may need to be smaller still, or something may need to change first. Not easy. Possible.
copy.commit_line: Any size is a real step. If it doesn't work, or the problem shifts, come back: problem-solving goes round more than once.
copy.commit_line_rehearse: A bigger step can help to rehearse before you take it.
copy.commit_line_safety: If it gets more dangerous, call now. You don't have to wait for a plan.
copy.conf_title: How sure are you that you could do the smallest version of this?
copy.decompose_title: Some parts of this are facts. Some are up to other people. Some are in your hands.
copy.feel_title: What's the feeling that's pointing at a problem?
copy.fo_ambiv-admitting-need-help: Asking for help or owning a mistake can feel like it makes you smaller. It's also a way of looking after what matters.
copy.fo_ambiv-change-might-not-help: If you change things and it still hurts, that would be hard. That fear is real. Staying put to avoid finding out is a choice too.
copy.fo_ambiv-hard-conversation: Hard conversations carry real risk. The question is whether not having it costs more than having it.
copy.fo_ambiv-losing-something: Change usually costs something. There may be a way to change and keep the part that matters.
copy.go_ambiv: Look at what it protects me from
copy.l_dear_man: Work out what to say with DEAR MAN
copy.l_missing_links: Find what got in the way
copy.l_others: This part is about them. Work out what to say with DEAR MAN
copy.mine_q: Which of these are in your hands?
copy.not_fit_facts: When something isn't clear yet, it helps to get the facts straight before solving anything.
copy.not_fit_other: Problem Solve works from a feeling that's pointing at a problem you can work on. This one might want something else first.
copy.not_fit_shame: When a feeling says something is wrong with you, there's nothing there to solve. Lots of people feel this. Doing the opposite of hiding often helps more. If there's one thing you did that you want to put right, you can come back for that.
copy.not_now_line: That makes sense. When a feeling is this loud, planning is harder. It may help to bring it down a little first, then come back to this.
copy.others_title: Which parts are up to someone else?
copy.own_step_hint: Write it your way, or start from one of these.
copy.own_step_title: What's the step you already know you want to take?
copy.piling: It's not one thing. Everything feels like too much
copy.re_cant-afraid-aftermath: The fear of what comes after is real, and you can prepare for it. Rehearsing the hard part first can make the real thing less overwhelming.
copy.re_cant-ambivalent: That's honest. Both sides are real: the part that wants change and the part that doesn't. Let's look at what staying the same protects you from.
copy.re_cant-keep-putting-off: Putting it off usually protects you from something, like discomfort, failing or conflict. Let's find the smallest version of the step and see how sure you feel about that.
copy.re_cant-no-energy: That's not a flaw in you. When you're running low, even obvious steps feel impossible. Refill a little first, then come back.
copy.re_person-dont-know-what-to-say: DEAR MAN is for exactly that. It gives you a shape for what to say, so you don't start from nothing.
copy.re_person-no-right-to-speak: That feeling is worth a look. You have needs, and saying them isn't selfish. This may be more about your self-respect than the problem itself.
copy.re_person-scared-reaction: Their reaction is worth taking seriously. You can prepare what to say and rehearse how you'll handle the hard part.
copy.re_person-tried-they-dont-listen: When something hasn't landed, it may be the approach and not the message. Changing how you say it can change whether it gets through. Or this may be where your influence over them ends.
copy.re_tried-different-approaches: That tells you something. Either it needs a different kind of strategy, or this wall won't move and the wise move is to put your energy somewhere else.
copy.re_tried-exhausted: Trying hard without results wears you out. You're not failing, you're running low. The most useful thing now is to refill, not push harder.
copy.re_tried-talked-to-them: Maybe it's the approach that needs to change, not the goal. Saying your piece and saying it so it gets through are different things.
copy.re_tried-thinking-constantly: That's your mind working on it, and it counts. Thinking and doing are different skills. You've done the thinking. Let's try the smallest piece of doing.
copy.ready_title: Can you think about this fairly clearly right now, or is the feeling too loud?
copy.rest_line: Stopping here is a real choice. You can come back to this when you have more in the tank.
copy.review_done_line: You took the step and saw what it did. That's the whole loop: a problem, a step, and seeing how it went.
copy.review_help_title: You took the step. Did it help with the problem?
copy.review_next_didnt: That happens, and it's useful to know. What would help next time?
copy.review_next_didnt_safety: That happens. If you're not safe now, call. Or pick another way.
copy.review_next_nohelp: You did it, and it didn't help. That's worth knowing. What would help now?
copy.review_next_nohelp_safety: It didn't help enough. If you're not safe now, call. Or pick another way.
copy.review_next_part: Part of it is still a step. What would help with the rest?
copy.review_title: How did it go? You planned: {step}
copy.review_title_own: How did it go? You planned: {mine}
copy.solutions_title_mine: Here's what's in your hands. Which direction feels right?
copy.solutions_title_small: Let's start small. Which direction feels right?
copy.sub_title: Can you say a bit more?
copy.sub_title_tried: You've been trying. That counts, even though it hasn't landed the way you needed. Can you say a bit more?
copy.triage_title: When everything piles up, one thing is a foothold. Which would shift most if it moved even a little?
